Q: "Ordinal Not Found" with ComCtl32.lib A:

An additional #pragma comment fixes the issue:

#pragma comment(linker, R"("/manifestdependency:
                            type='win32'
                            name='Microsoft.Windows.Common-Controls'
                            version='6.0.0.0'
                            processorArchitecture='*'
                            publicKeyToken='6595b64144ccf1df'
                            language='*'")")

Sources:

  • Raymond Chen: The Old New Thing blog,
  • Microsoft Learn link from the previous blog (see the end of the section).

Q: Docs for setupCommands in vscode cppdbg launch json A:

Navigate to GDB's bin directory and run gdb.exe. You will see the (gdb) prompt, Type help and hit Enter to see the list of classes of commands. Type help <class> and hit Enter to see the list of commands of a particular class. Type help all and hit Enter to print out all commands (big listing, not recommended). Finally, type help <command> and hit Enter to get detailed description. Example:

(gdb) help data
...
set print elements -- Set limit on array elements to print.
...
set print repeats -- Set threshold for repeated print elements.
...

(gdb) help set print elements
Set limit on array elements to print.
"unlimited" causes there to be no limit.
This setting also applies to string chars when "print characters"
is set to "elements".

(gdb) help set print repeats
Set threshold for repeated print elements.
"unlimited" causes all elements to be individually printed.

Q: A regular expression to match C-style string literals A:

The Standard C-Style Strings Regex

# Demo - 
# PCRE :  https://regex101.com/r/egWitL/1/substitution
# Python :  https://regex101.com/r/egWitL/2/substitution
# Dot-Net :  https://regex101.com/r/egWitL/3/substitution
# Java :  https://regex101.com/r/egWitL/4/substitution
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# JScript :  https://regex101.com/r/egWitL/5/substitution
# (?:(?:/\*[^*]*\*+?(?:[^/*][^*]*\*+)*/|//(?:[^\\]|\\(?:\r?\n)?)*?(?:\r?\n|$))|(?!(?<!\\)(?:"[^"\\]*(?:\\[\S\s][^"\\]*)*"|'[^'\\]*(?:\\[\S\s][^'\\]*)*'))[\S\s][^/"'\\]*)*(?:(?<!\\)("[^"\\]*(?:\\[\S\s][^"\\]*)*"|'[^'\\]*(?:\\[\S\s][^'\\]*)*')|[\S\s]+)


# The Goal is to match all the way up to strings
# then the string itself or to EOS. Every char is matched.
# This enables making a list of just the strings, skipping comments etc ...
# Can be demonstrated by replacing each match with :  '$1\n'

(?>
   (?:                              # Skip / consume  -  Comments 
      /\*                              # Start /* .. */ comment
      [^*]* \*+?
      (?: [^/*] [^*]* \*+ )*
      /                                # End /* .. */ comment
    | 
      //                               # Start // comment
      (?:                              # Possible line-continuation
         [^\\] 
       | \\ 
         (?: \r? \n )?
      )*?
      (?: \r? \n | $ )
   )
 | 
   (?!
      (?<! \\ )
      (?:
         "
         [^"\\]* 
         (?: \\ [\S\s] [^"\\]* )*
         "
       | '
         [^'\\]* 
         (?: \\ [\S\s] [^'\\]* )*
         '
      )
   )
   [\S\s]                           # Pass through for unhandled chars [/"'\\]
   [^/"'\\]*                        # Skip / consume - Chars which doesn't start a comment, string, escape,
)*

(?>                              # Non - comments  :   Strings
   (?<! \\ )                        # Safety - If a C-file can be parsed as valid, this won't happen. 
   (                                # (1 start)
      "
      [^"\\]*                          # Double quoted text
      (?: \\ [\S\s] [^"\\]* )*
      "
    | '
      [^'\\]*                          # Single quoted text
      (?: \\ [\S\s] [^'\\]* )*
      ' 
   )                                # (1 end)
 | 
   [\S\s]+                          # To EOS - no other strings found,
                                    #  consume the remaining chars in the sample
)

Using VERBS

  # Demo - 
  # PCRE / Perl :   https://regex101.com/r/whSbyz/1
  
  (?:                              # Comments 
     /\*                              # Start /* .. */ comment
     [^*]* \*+?
     (?: [^/*] [^*]* \*+ )*
     /                                # End /* .. */ comment
   | 
     //                               # Start // comment
     (?:                              # Possible line-continuation
        [^\\] 
      | \\ 
        (?: \r? \n )?
     )*?
     (?: \r? \n | $ )
  )
  (*SKIP) (*FAIL)                  # Skip Comments
| 
  (?:                              # Non - comments 
     (?<! \\ )                        # If a C-file can be parsed, this won't happen
     (                                # (1 start)
        "
        [^"\\]*                          # Double quoted text
        (?: \\ [\S\s] [^"\\]* )*
        "
      | '
        [^'\\]*                          # Single quoted text
        (?: \\ [\S\s] [^'\\]* )*
        ' 
     )                                # (1 end), Any other char
   | 
     [\S\s] 
     [^/"'\\]*                        # Skip Chars which doesn't start a comment, string, escape,
     (*SKIP) (*FAIL)                  # or line continuation (escape + newline)
  )

Q: Windows task scheduler error 101 launch failure code 2147943785 A:

The user that is configured to run this scheduled task must have "Log on as a batch job" rights on the computer that hosts the exe you are launching. This can be configured on the local security policy of the computer that hosts the exe, but requires that you be logged in as a local administrator. While logged in as a local administrator, you can change the policy (on the server hosting the exe) under:

Administrative Tools -> Local Security Policy -> Local Policies -> User Rights Assignment -> Log On As Batch Job

Add your user to this list (you could also make the user account a local admin on the machine hosting the exe).

Finally, you could also simply copy your exe from the network location to your local computer and run it from there instead.

Note also that a domain policy could be restricting "Log on as a batch job" rights at your organization.
